segments.text:
The comment gives the task and the reason.
- Task: run the line of `like.spec` twice, each time from an idle machine.
- Reason: in go.sh every bwx12 process started about 5 s after other 120-thread work. The earlier runs of this line started from an idle machine.
- `w120-R8` and `w120-w120-F72d12` are the result folders of those earlier runs. Each of the two folders holds 5 launch lines. The first one has the arguments of `like.spec`. These two launch lines show the 1-minute load averages 0.00 and 0.34 [Ref5].
- `Idle` here means a 1-minute load average below 1.0.
segments.heading: Header comment: why this control exists

segments.text: `set -u`: the script stops when it uses a variable that was never set. The script does not use `set -e`. So a failed command does not stop it. Each check below calls `fail` by itself.

Paths on CRB, two expected checksums and the expected boot id. All six values are equal to those in go.sh.
- `D`: the folder that holds `like.spec`. `RX`: the runner script `rx.sh`. `BW`: the binary bwx12.
- `SHA`: the sha256 that the file bwx12 must have. `RXSHA`: the sha256 that `rx.sh` must have.
- `BOOT`: the boot id that the running system must have.

Prints one line that starts with `==` and the label given as argument. It only reports. It stops nothing. The line holds:
- the UTC time and the boot id
- the `MemTotal` line of `/proc/meminfo` (`tr -s ' '` reduces each run of spaces to one space)
- the content of `/proc/loadavg`: the three load averages, the runnable tasks and all tasks as `1/1013`, and the newest process id [Ref7]
- the number of logins: `who` prints one line per login, and `wc -l` counts the lines
- `present` or `absent` for the file `/tmp/positron-perf.RUNNING`
- the number of processes of each user: `ps -eo user=` prints the user of every process, and `sort | uniq -c` counts equal lines
segments.heading: Function `state`: print one state line

segments.text: Prints `FAILED:` and the message. Then it prints a state line with the label `abort`. Then it ends go2.sh with exit status 1. Every failed check of go2.sh ends here, and no later step runs.
segments.heading: Function `fail`: stop the run

segments.text:
Prints the process id of go2.sh and a command that stops the run.
- `kill -TERM -- -<pid>` sends the termination signal to every process of the process group with that number.
- This stops go2.sh and its child processes only when go2.sh is the leader of its process group. go2.sh does not make itself the leader.
- In the rerun the start command ran go2.sh through the tool `setsid` [Ref10]. This tool starts a program as the leader of a new process group [Ref11]. So go2.sh was the leader in the rerun.

Check of the marker file.
- Test: does the file `/tmp/positron-perf.RUNNING` exist.
- On failure (the file exists): `fail` stops the run with `RUNNING file present`.
- `waitidle` (line 25) tests the file again at each of its tries. `rx.sh` tests it before the process and once per second while the process runs [Ref2].
- Purpose: go2.sh does not say who creates the file or what the file stands for.
segments.heading: Checks before the run

segments.text:
Lock against a second run.
- `exec 9> ...` opens the file `go-T72.lock` for writing as file descriptor 9 of the shell. It creates the file when it is missing.
- Test: `flock -n 9` asks for an exclusive lock on that file and does not wait.
- On failure (another process holds the lock, or the lock file could not be opened): `fail` stops the run with `another go.sh holds the lock`.
- Purpose, by the message `another go.sh holds the lock`: go2.sh must not run at the same time as go.sh. go.sh uses the same lock file. A second go2.sh would fail here too.
- The lock lasts as long as file descriptor 9 is open: until go2.sh and the child processes that inherited it have ended.

Checksum checks of `rx.sh` (line 18) and of the binary bwx12 (line 19).
- Test: `sha256sum -c -` reads one line `checksum  path` from `echo`, computes the sha256 of that file and compares the two values. Its report goes to `/dev/null`, which discards it.
- On failure (the content differs, or the file cannot be read): `fail` stops the run.
- Purpose, by the messages: the two files must be the script and the binary of 2026-11-15.
- Cross-check: the build record of bwx12 lists the value of `SHA` for the file `bwx12` [Ref4]. The binary itself is not in the local folders. The local copy of `rx.sh` has the value of `RXSHA` (computed with `sha256sum` on 2026-11-21) [Ref2].

File check.
- Test: `like.spec` exists and is not empty (`-s`).
- On failure: `fail` with `missing <path>`.
- go2.sh does not test the checksum of `like.spec`. In the rerun the `launch` lines of the two control processes hold the arguments of the local `like.spec` (compared with `diff` on 2026-11-21) [Ref6].

Boot check.
- Test: the boot id of the running system is equal to `BOOT` (line 12).
- On failure: `fail` stops the run.
- Purpose, by the message: the run must happen in the boot that was checked at 12 modules and 7200 MT/s.
- The check compares the boot id only. It does not read the memory speed or the number of modules.

Memory size check.
- Test: `awk` prints the second field of the `MemTotal` line of `/proc/meminfo`, a value in kB. The value must be 395000000 kB or more.
- On failure: `fail` stops the run.
- Purpose, by the message: a lower value means `not 12 modules`. The script does not say how the limit was chosen.
- In the rerun each of the 6 state lines shows 395392808 kB [Ref1].

`rxok NAME` reads the file `launches.txt` of the newest result folder `w120-NAME-<time>`. Its text is equal to `rxok` in go.sh.
- `ls -d ... | tail -1` lists the matching files in name order and keeps the last one. The time in the folder name puts the newest folder last.
- The function succeeds only when a file was found, the file holds exactly 1 line that starts with `rc `, and it holds exactly 1 line that starts with `rc 0 `.
- `rx.sh` writes one line `rc <exit status> <tag>` per process. It ends with status 0 also when bwx12 failed [Ref2].
segments.heading: Function `rxok`: did the bwx12 process end with status 0

segments.text:
Tries up to 180 times:
- When the marker file exists, `fail` stops the run.
- `awk` reads `/proc/loadavg`. When the first field (the 1-minute load average) is below 1.0, `awk` ends with status 0 and the function returns. The run goes on.
- If not, the function sleeps 5 s and tries again.
- After 180 tries (180 x 5 s = 15 min) `fail` stops the run.
- The test reads the 1-minute value only. It does not test the 5-minute value or the number of runnable tasks.
segments.heading: Function `waitidle`: wait for an idle machine

segments.text:
Runs the same steps twice, with the names `T72I1` and `T72I2`.
- Line 28: `waitidle` (line 25) waits for a 1-minute load average below 1.0.
- Line 29: a state line records the machine state at that moment.
- Line 30: `rx.sh` runs one bwx12 process with the arguments of `like.spec` [Ref3]. The spec file is the input of `rx.sh`. On a non-zero exit status of `rx.sh`: `fail` stops the run.
- Line 31: when `rxok` (line 23) does not succeed, `fail` stops the run.
- Line 32: a state line after the process.
- `rx.sh` adds its own wait before the launch: until at most 2 tasks are runnable (at most 40 s), then 5 s [Ref2]. When more than 2 tasks are still runnable after the 40 s, `rx.sh` starts the process anyway. So bwx12 starts 5 s or more after the idle test.
segments.heading: Two control processes

segments.text: Final state line with the label `end`, then the word `ALLDONE`. The script reaches these lines only when no check called `fail`.
